verdicts.summary: A per-thread sweep and a full sweep can both dispatch thread.auto-settle for the same thread. The Orchestrator rejects the second one because settledOverride is already set, so the thread cannot be settled twice. The only cost is a warning log.
verdicts.scenario: A full sweep and the thread's own sweep both pick thread T as a candidate and both dispatch thread.auto-settle with the same snapshotAt. The first settles T. The second finds settledOverride === 'settled' and fails with OrchestratorDispatchError. settleThread catches that and logs 'automatic thread settlement skipped'. I also tried an event arriving while T's sweep waits for a permit: the state is 'queued' or 'rerun', so enqueueThread returns void (:555-557) and no second fiber starts.

verdicts.summary: With `merge --auto`, the read when the command ends sees the PR still open. The run-end read still fires and bypasses the cache, so the merge is still picked up.
verdicts.scenario: An agent runs `gh pr merge --auto`. The command ends, its id goes into `ended`, and refreshOpenLinks is called; the PR is still open. Later run.updated arrives with status completed. closeCommands.delete returns true, so refreshOpenLinks runs again. requestSync puts the link in `requested`, and readGroup calls invalidate before reading the summary (:347-348), so the second read is fresh. A repeat turn-item.updated for the same id is ignored at :540.

verdicts.summary: Only a completion that stays 'ready' for the whole 2s now notifies. Before, the completion timestamp was kept from the prior state, so one 'ready' observation was enough. If a thread's runtime goes to 'idle' (which shows as 'waiting') right after a run completes, the pending notification is cancelled and never sent. I could not confirm that the runtime goes idle after completion.
verdicts.scenario: 1. A run completes and the thread is observed as ready + completed, so the gate arms a timer (logic.ts:57). 2. Within 2s the thread's runtime.status becomes 'idle', which resolveSidebarThreadStatus maps to 'waiting' (Sidebar.logic.ts:911-912). That makes settled false, and cancel runs (logic.ts:42). 3. The thread stays idle, so no 'Thread completed' notification arrives. The old code (diff lines 1191-1205) kept prior.completion and would have notified at step 1. I also tried a repeat observation with the same completedAt while pending; logic.ts:55 stops a duplicate timer.
verdicts.missing: Whether the client thread shell's runtime.status becomes 'idle' after a completed run. That depends on how provider sessions map onto the shell runtime, which I did not trace. The provider adapters do emit 'idle' provider-thread statuses (CodexAdapterV2.ts:866, ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:1692).

verdicts.summary: When the hold expires, the timer bumps the tracker's version and notifies listeners. Both clients read the version (web through clockKey, mobile through useMemo deps), so observe runs again and the thread is no longer working.
verdicts.scenario: Thread T stops at t0 and nothing else changes. At t0+2s the timer sets state.working = false, stamps the return time, does version++ and calls the listeners. On web, useSyncExternalStore re-renders and clockKey changes, so partitionSidebarThreads runs observe again. Its previous.working is false, so T goes to `active`. On mobile, the inboxVersion dep makes useMemo call observe again. Both mobile callers (HomeScreen and ThreadNavigationSidebar) share one tracker and both pass the full thread list.

verdicts.summary: A thread that is snoozed, archived or pinned when it stops working leaves the Working shelf at once, and its return time is stamped at the stop. When the timer fires early and nothing has expired, it only re-arms and bumps the version.
verdicts.scenario: Thread T is working and gets snoozed in the same observation in which it stops. excluded is true, so deadline is null and working is false. Because previous.working was true, the return time is set to `at` (:220). I also tried the timer firing a little early: no deadline is <= at, so schedule() re-arms with Math.max(0, next-now). That causes one extra re-render with no state change.

verdicts.summary: The deadline is set once per stop and cannot be pushed later by repeat observations. A real resume clears it, and the next stop starts a new 2s hold.
verdicts.scenario: T stops at t0, so deadline is t0+2000. Observations at t0+500 and t0+1500 reuse previous.deadline, so the deadline stays where it was. If T resumes at t0+1000, actual is true, the deadline becomes null and T is really working. If T then stops at t0+1200, a new deadline of t0+3200 is set. The hold is still bounded to 2s after each real stop.
